d: Proximity Prompts allow users to trigger actions when they approach objects in the 3D space.
h:
ProximityPrompt objects encourage user interaction to trigger an action when they approach in-game objects such as doors, light switches, and buttons. Using this object, you can:

  • Indicate what objects a user can interact with in the game.
  • Display the action a user can take on the object, then trigger the action through user input such as pressing or holding a key.
  • Display the correct input for all input types, such a keyboard, gamepad, and touchscreen keys.

See the Dungeon Delve sample place for the fully working proximity prompt examples shown in the video above.

Create proximity prompts

You must parent proximity prompts to the part, model, or attachment that you want a user to interact with. To add a proximity prompt to a BasePart, Model, or Attachment object:

  1. In the Explorer window, hover over the BasePart, Model, or Attachment and click the ⊕ button. A contextual menu displays.
  2. From the menu, insert a ProximityPrompt.

Customize proximity prompts

You can customize a proximity prompt based on how you want it to appear, when you want it to be visible, and what you want a user to do to trigger the action.

Appearance

Proximity prompts need to communicate three things:

  • The object that a user can interact with.
  • The action that triggers when they interact with the proximity prompt.
  • The key that a user must press or hold.

You can specify these through the following properties:

  • ObjectText An optional name for the object a user can interact with.
  • ActionText An optional name for the action a user will trigger.
  • KeyboardKeyCode The keyboard key a user must press or hold to trigger the action.
  • GamepadKeyCode The gamepad key a user must press or hold to trigger the action.

Visibility

You can control when the proximity prompt is visible through its MaxActivationDistance, RequiresLineOfSight, and Exclusivity properties.

MaxActivationDistance

The MaxActivationDistance property allows you to define the range from around the ProximityPrompt object that activates the visibility of the proximity prompt. Once a user's character enters that range, the proximity prompt becomes visible.

RequiresLineOfSight

The RequiresLineOfSight property activates the visibility of the proximity prompt when there's a clear path from the camera to the ProximityPrompt object. By default, this property is set to true.

Exclusivity

If a user's character is within range of multiple proximity prompts, each proximity prompt's visibility depends on which proximity prompt the camera is pointing at, as well as each proximity prompt's Exclusivity property value.

Interactivity

You can customize how a user interacts with a proximity prompt through its HoldDuration and ClickablePrompt properties.

HoldDuration

The HoldDuration property determines how many seconds a user has to press a key before the proximity prompt's action triggers. If this property has a value of 0, the proximity prompt's action triggers immediately.

ClickablePrompt

The ClickablePrompt property specifies if a user can click on a proximity prompt to trigger its action. When set to true, a user can interact with the proximity prompt by directly clicking the proximity prompt or by pressing the specified key. When set to false, a user can only interact with the proximity prompt by pressing the specified key.

Note that if a user is using a phone or a tablet, they can always interact with the proximity prompt by directly clicking the proximity prompt regardless of the ClickablePrompt property's value.

Script proximity prompts

You can connect to proximity prompt events either on the ProximityPrompt object itself or globally through ProximityPromptService. The ProximityPromptService allows you to manage all proximity prompt behavior from one location, preventing any need for duplicate code in your game.

Event Description
PromptTriggered Fires when a player interacts with a proximity prompt (after the duration for a prompt with non-zero HoldDuration).
PromptTriggerEnded Triggers when the player stops interacting with a proximity prompt.
PromptButtonHoldBegan Fires when a player begins interacting with a proximity prompt with a non-zero HoldDuration value.
PromptButtonHoldEnded Fires when a player stops interacting with a proximity prompt with a non-zero HoldDuration value.
PromptShown Triggers in LocalScripts when a proximity prompt is made visible.
PromptHidden Triggers in LocalScripts when a prompt is hidden.

The following code sample includes a basic framework for using ProximityPromptService:

local ProximityPromptService = game:GetService("ProximityPromptService")

-- Detect when prompt is triggered
local function onPromptTriggered(promptObject, player)

end

-- Detect when prompt hold begins
local function onPromptHoldBegan(promptObject, player)

end

-- Detect when prompt hold ends
local function onPromptHoldEnded(promptObject, player)

end

-- Connect prompt events to handling functions
ProximityPromptService.PromptTriggered:Connect(onPromptTriggered)
ProximityPromptService.PromptButtonHoldBegan:Connect(onPromptHoldBegan)
ProximityPromptService.PromptButtonHoldEnded:Connect(onPromptHoldEnded)

kid.simple: A `ProximityPrompt` is the little pop-up that appears when you walk up to something, like "E  Open Door". It shows players what they can interact with and which key to press. It automatically shows the right button for keyboards, gamepads, and touch screens. You add it to a part and then use a script to decide what happens when it is triggered.
kid.analogy: It is like a shop door that lights up a sign saying "Push" when you get close. The sign tells you what to do, and the door only opens when you actually push.
keyPoints: Put a `ProximityPrompt` inside the `BasePart`, `Model`, or `Attachment` players should interact with.
`ObjectText` names the thing ("Door"), `ActionText` names the action ("Open"), and `KeyboardKeyCode`/`GamepadKeyCode` set the keys.
`MaxActivationDistance` sets how close the character must be before the prompt appears.
`RequiresLineOfSight` (on by default) hides the prompt if something blocks the camera's view of it.
`Exclusivity` decides what happens when several prompts are close: one per key, only one at all, or always show all.
`HoldDuration` sets how many seconds the key must be held; 0 means a quick press works.
`ClickablePrompt` lets players click the prompt itself; on phones and tablets it can always be tapped.
Listen for `Triggered` on one prompt, or use `ProximityPromptService.PromptTriggered` to handle all prompts in one place.

terms.proximity: How close you are to something.
terms.MaxActivationDistance: The distance, in studs, from the prompt where it appears. At 10, the prompt shows when your character is within 10 studs.
terms.line of sight: A clear, unblocked view. If a wall is between the camera and the prompt, there is no line of sight.
terms.Exclusivity: Rules for which prompts show when several are nearby. `OneGlobally` shows only the one you are looking at.
terms.keycode: The name of a specific key or button, like `Enum.KeyCode.E`.
terms.HoldDuration: Seconds the key must be held. 2 means press and hold for 2 seconds.
terms.trigger: To set off the prompt's action, by pressing (or holding) the key or tapping it.

example.title: Open a door with a prompt
example.place: Script inside a ProximityPrompt that is inside a part named Door
example.code:
local prompt = script.Parent
local door = prompt.Parent

prompt.ObjectText = "Door"
prompt.ActionText = "Open"
prompt.KeyboardKeyCode = Enum.KeyCode.E
prompt.HoldDuration = 0.5 -- hold E for half a second
prompt.MaxActivationDistance = 10 -- show within 10 studs

local function onTriggered(player)
	print(player.Name .. " opened the door")
	-- Let players walk through and make the door see-through
	door.CanCollide = false
	door.Transparency = 0.7
	prompt.Enabled = false

	task.wait(3)

	-- Close it again
	door.CanCollide = true
	door.Transparency = 0
	prompt.Enabled = true
end

prompt.Triggered:Connect(onTriggered)
explain: The script sits in the prompt, and the prompt sits in the door part.
We set the text, key, hold time, and distance so the prompt reads "Door / Open" and needs E held for half a second.
When triggered, the server gets the player who used it and opens the door by turning off collisions and fading it.
We hide the prompt while open, wait 3 seconds, then close the door and show the prompt again.

watchOut: A prompt placed in Workspace by itself will not show up. It must be inside a part, model, or attachment.
With `AlwaysShow`, every visible prompt using the same key fires at once. Use different keys or a different `Exclusivity`.
If the prompt never appears, check `MaxActivationDistance` and whether a wall is blocking the line of sight.
Do important game changes (like opening doors for everyone) in a server `Script`, not a `LocalScript`.
